title: Blue Notebook Review - BING BONG!
description:
Your Community Engagement Team is back with an update covering the last week in February. 

Tune in for tips on safe driving, info on the HLP Team and their outreach/enforcement efforts and hear from NRO Hollowell "forthwith"!
transcript_text: Hello Santa Monica. My name is Sergeant Rick with the Santa Monica Police Department and this is your Blue Notebook review. Seems like y'all go against every algorithm that say short videos are the way to go because last week's video didn't do too well. So maybe you do like the added commentary. And if there's one thing I can do is talk. So let's throw the clock out the window and just have a conversation about what happened last week. Oh, and before we get started, did you know that in the month of February, 50% of the total calls for service were officers selfinitiated? Which means, unlike the fire department, we don't wait for a radio call to take action. And before you get in the comments, oh, the fire department's America's heroes, we do have a friendly and healthy rivalry with our fire department. It's just that we beat them in in every thing that we do, every softball game, every event, every activity. We just always win. So, now they've got that out of the way. Uh, let's get right into the crime stats with your beat one neighborhood resource officer, Officer Hollowell. Officer Hollowell, talk to us. Thanks, Sergeant Rick. Officer Steven Hollowell here, your beat one neighborhood resource officer for the pier, the beach, and the promot where I'm at right now. And for this operational period, I will be discussing crime suppression as I usually do. The Santa Monica Police responded to 2,698 calls for service as well as conducted 114 arrests. Great job, boys and girls. Way to work the beat. I'll be discussing two items or incidents that occurred. Santa Monica police responded to a call for service that involved a person who stole from a convenience store and also struck the victim with a stick. The police responded and a short foot pursuit ensued. After the foot pursuit, the suspect was taken into custody without incident. Post haste, bing bong, straight to jail. As for the second incident, Santa Monica police working the smart center were able to obtain that a U-Haul's truck was stolen. They directed the officers to the appropriate place where the U-Haul truck was. A felony stop ensued and both suspects were taken into custody forth and they were arrested for driving a stolen vehicle or operating a stolen vehicle. And that's it. Back to you in the studio, Sergeant Rick. >> Thanks, Officer Hollowell. And great work by the by the men and women in blue. That's another week of over a 100 arrests. Sam Monica, if if you if you seen a difference in the streets, I would say let's go back from December to now, can you put in the comments below and see uh so we can see if the work we're doing is making an impact because we think it is since we're out there all the time. I want to hear from you guys, from the general public to see if if you're seeing a difference in the streets or uh if there's another area, a little problem area that you know of that we haven't addressed yet, put that in the comments below, too, and we'll let the right people know to send the right officers out there and make a difference. And then let's head over to your B3 neighborhood resource officer, Officer Tago, or as my mom would call him, Officer Dodo. And no disrespect, Tago, it's just English wasn't her first language. Imagine growing up and thinking wallpaper was paper wall or that oatmeal is hot cereal. Yeah, that whole oatmeal hot cereal thing. I didn't realize that until I think 3 years ago. Literally been calling it hot cereal my whole life. All right, Toggle, what do you got? >> Thanks, Arch. Aloha, Santa Monica. Officer Toggle here, your B3 neighborhood resource officer. Our homeless lay program officers responded to 262 radio calls, conducted 221 self initiated contacts, addressed 12 encampments, made 23 arrest, and issued 31 citations. Great job team. And here's your instant of note. During enforcement activity along Freeway embankments, officers contacted a Santa Monica native who was experiencing homelessness. Working with outreach partners, officers assisted the individual with placement into Samuel Shell temporary housing where he is now working toward permanent housing. Situations like this highlight the balance of the work enforcement when necessary while also creating opportunities for individuals to connect with services and housing. We'll continue staying present in the community and working alongside our partners to address issues as they come up. I just want to give a quick shout out to Mama Verbeck. Thank you for calling me Officer Dodo. I appreciate it. And back to you in the studio, Sarge. [laughter] Thanks, Tago. Uh I love seeing how the enforcement side and the compassion side uh to those who need it work hand in hand. And let's head over to your beat two in a row. Officer Partardo. Izzy, what do you got for us? >> All right, Santa Monica, let's skip the warm-up and get right into it. This week, officers conducted 486 traffic stop and issued 353 citations as part of an ongoing traffic safety efforts across the city. During a traffic stop near the main street area, officers discovered a concealed loaded ghost gun inside a vehicle with multiple passengers. The owner admitted it was his and was arrested without incident. Officers also conducted a grant-f funed distracted driving operation, resulting in 38 citations with 24 of those being cell phone violations. Did you know taking your eyes off the road for just 5 seconds at 55 mph is like driving the length of a football field blindfolded? So maybe next time that text can wait. And with St. Patrick's Day coming up. Our traffic enforcement team will be hosting a know your limits event to help educate the public and remind everyone that celebrating responsibly is the best way to avoid celebrating in the back of a patrol vehicle. Drive say Santa Monica. Back to you in the studio, Sergeant Rick. >> Ooh, another gun off the streets. Great work. I know. I didn't know that stat about taking your eyes off the road for 5 seconds. That really puts things into perspective. So, please stay off your phone while you're driving. It's not worth it. And then let's close it out with your beat four in a row officer Aila to talk to us about the community engagement we've done uh last week. And Brandon, it's good to see that you're still with us. Go for it. Thank you, sir. Hello, Blue Notebook family. Today I'm on the rooftop with one of our real time crime center operators, David. David, how you doing? How you doing, sir? >> Good. Good. Hey, so I tried to get in to the Smart Center a couple weeks ago. had a little hit. Could you hook it up today? >> I heard what you did last time and I don't think I can do that. I don't want to get in trouble. Fair enough. During this reporting period, community engagement team continued to meet with neighborhood and business groups. We also conducted multiple security assessments. In regard to our youth engagement, we played soccer with the Autobond Soccer Club at Lincoln Middle School. We also played kickball with students from Franklin Elementary. We are still undefeated, 2 and 0. So if any school wants us to come out there, please give us a call. So with that said, our next upcoming event is Wagwatch at Douglas Park, March 25th at 6:00 p.m. Hope to see you there. Actually, Brandon, we're 3 and 0. Much like how we don't lose to the fire department, we're not going to lose to a bunch of kids. But the kids actually do take it better than the fire department does. Anyhow, future Rick, if you could put the flyer up for the wagon watch. We'll see you there, Douglas Park. Bring your pet. We'll bring the coffee and let's have a conversation. No agenda. And that, my friends, concludes this week's Blue Notebook Review. Remember, focus on what's right in front of you, and you'll find plenty worth believing in. See you next week. Thanks, Sergeant Rick. Officer Steven Hollow here, your neighborhood resource officer for Beat One. >> [screaming and laughter] >> That was great.
